newsitem.title: GERMANY: Top German ad executive looks to U.S.-style system.
newsitem.headline: Top German ad executive looks to U.S.-style system.

text.p: One of Germany's top advertising executives said on Wednesday the national television market was hamstrung by ad regulations which needed to be lifted if the country hoped to improve programming.

In a speech at the Munich Advertising Conference, Willi Schalk, chief executive of advertising giant McCann-Erickson's German unit, called U.S. television a prime example of the superior programming and ads that appear in a "freer" system.

"Deregulation goes along with freedom, a market economy, democracy," Schalk said. "I am not afraid of it because I have seen how it has worked in the U.S. for 50 years without these stifling regulations."

Schalk showed industry members at the conference a 1986 ad from an American network about the value of advertising to fund more diverse TV programming, which he said illustrated how far German industry had to go in developing acceptance of TV ads.

"At the time this American ad appeared, the German industry had just introduced private television," Schalk said. "Can you imagine such an ad in Germany? For some dreams, one must wait 10 years, or maybe longer."
Schalk was the first German chief executive to serve in the New York advertising market, serving until 1989 as president of U.S. ad giant BBDO Worldwide.

He reiterated calls he had made on Monday in an interview with Reuters to lift restrictions on advertising on public television, during news programming and on the length and frequency of commercial breaks on private stations.
"Who are we trying to protect with these rules?" Schalk asked. "Is it the consumer? Is it possible that (private companies) might understand more about the public's wishes than bureaucrats?"

German public broadcasters fund part of their programming with ads, but they are limited to 20 minutes per day and cannot appear after 8 p.m. or on Sunday. News broadcasts on public or private stations are also not allowed to break for ads.
